name: Diesel air heater (parking heater)

fuels: diesel (EN 590, a grade suited to the cold)
combustion.note: Safe indoors only with intake and exhaust piped outside and sealed. Needs 12 or 24 V DC: start-up draws about 75–100 W (Webasto 75 W; Espar 8.3 A at 12 V), then roughly 10–40 W running on the 2–4 kW units; Autoterm rates its AIR-8D at up to 75–90 W and its AIR-9D at up to 210–290 W.

comps.spec: Diesel left in the heater's own tank or the vehicle tank it draws from; check for water and sludge before use
comps.loc: Separate heater tank, or the vehicle tank via a standpipe

comps.spec: Separate small fuel tank with a pickup through the top
comps.loc: Beside the heater or under the floor

comps.spec: Fuel metering (dosing) pump: small pulse-driven 12 or 24 V pump that clicks as it runs; never run it on steady DC or the coil burns
comps.loc: Near the fuel tank on a rubber mount

comps.spec: Glow pin (ceramic on Webasto), a hot-surface igniter that heats the burner before fuel flows; the whole heater draws about 8 A at 12 V (Espar D2/D4) or 75 W (Webasto) during that start. Hot enough to burn
comps.loc: Side of the combustion chamber, under the cover

comps.spec: One 12 or 24 V motor turning two blower wheels: combustion air and warm air; air flow about 48 cfm (D2) to 85 cfm (D4) at full output
Control unit with temperature sensing and low and high voltage cut-outs (Espar: 10.5 V and 16 V at 12 V)
comps.loc: End of the heater under the cover

comps.spec: Overheat and flame sensors (temperature sensors) that shut the heater down
2 mm-bore nylon fuel line with rubber joiners, 25 mm combustion-air hose, and 60–90 mm warm-air duct rated for heat
comps.loc: Under the floor and behind panels

comps.spec: Control panel: a rotary knob, or an LCD timer and thermostat
comps.loc: Cab, bunk or living area wall

comps.spec: Blade fuse in a weatherproof holder close to the battery (within about 35 cm / 14 in): 15 A on the Webasto Air Top 2000 STC, 20 A on the Espar Airtronic D2 (12 V), 25 A in Autoterm's wiring diagrams; never swap in another rating or a wire

comps.loc: From battery to heater, heater to pump and panel

buildings.loc: Sleeper trucks (bunk heaters under the bunk or in a side box), vans and motorhomes
Motorhomes and camper vans; spares in the parts room
Cabin boats, under bunks and in lockers
Boats in stock and the parts counter
Converted vans and RVs left on site
Sleeper trucks parked at truck stops
Vans and trucks in for work

notes: Sealed combustion: the heater can sit inside a vehicle or room only because its combustion air, exhaust and fuel connections are all outside, with an airtight gasket between (Espar D2/D4). The exhaust runs up to 500 °C (Autoterm Air). Several cheap Chinese-made units have been turned back at the UK border for missing installation instructions and exhaust warnings (OPSS Vevor 2302-0090, OPSS Vevor 2212-0144). Diesel only: Autoterm says to use only EN 590 diesel, and Espar bans blending used engine oil into it; petrol belongs in no diesel heater (Autoterm Air, Espar D2/D4). Do not run one where flammable vapour, gas or lots of dust can collect, such as a garage holding petrol or solvents (Espar D2/D4, Autoterm Air).
